1. Isabel does NOT prioritize tasks  and

B) From "If either Isabel meets deadlines or she prioritizes tasks (but not both) then she manages projects" (contraposed): if she does NOT manage projects, then the antecedent is false, so she does NEITHER meet deadlines NOR prioritizes tasks (or both at once, but our inputs exclude both having when we already know she does not prioritize tasks). E) From "If either Isabel appreciates elegance OR she creates luxurious experiences (but not both), then she has a sophisticated style" (contraposed): if she does NOT have a sophisticated style, then the antecedent is false, so she does NEITHER appreciate elegance NOR create luxurious experiences.
Hence she does NOT create luxurious experiences.

F) From "Either Isabel does not have refined taste OR she creates luxurious experiences", this is equivalent to: if she has refined taste, then she creates luxurious experiences (👈 contraposed from nothing → she creates.), and we have already shown she does NOT create luxurious experiences. By modus tollens, she does NOT have refined taste.

Therefore Isabel does NOT have refined taste.
